clarification.title: Configure Workflow Units
clarification.description: Specify which successful workflow events qualify and how usage should be measured.

questions.label: Event name
questions.description: The exact event your app will send, for example vector.workflow.completed.

questions.label: Success condition
questions.description: The metadata key and value that identify a successful workflow.

questions.label: How should usage be measured?
questions.description: Count charges one unit per qualifying workflow. Sum totals a numeric metadata property.

options.label: Count events
options.description: Each successful workflow equals one Workflow Unit.

options.label: Sum a numeric property
options.description: Total a numeric metadata value from successful workflows.

questions.label: Numeric property, if summing
questions.description: Required only if you chose Sum.

questions.label: Display unit
questions.description: How the meter quantity should be labeled. Scalar is the standard default.

messages.text:
Help me choose: explain the remaining questions in plain language. Keep my original task and the details I already provided.
My answers so far:
Event name: vector.workflow.completed
Success condition: status = success
Numeric property, if summing: compute_units
Display unit: Scalar

Choose how to measure Workflow Units
Count events charges 1 Workflow Unit for each successful workflow. Sum a numeric property charges the event’s compute_units value, so larger workflows can use more units. Your event filter remains vector.workflow.completed with status = success, and the display unit remains Scalar.
How should successful workflows be measured? Choices: Count events; Sum compute_units.

questions.label: How should successful workflows be measured?
questions.description: Choose Count for one unit per successful workflow, or Sum to total compute_units from each successful event.

options.label: Count events

options.label: Sum compute_units
options.description: Each successful workflow uses the numeric compute_units value reported by the event.

messages.text:
Details for Choose how to measure Workflow Units:
How should successful workflows be measured?: Sum compute_units
Workflow Units is saved and verified: vector.workflow.completed AND metadata status = success, summed by compute_units, with Scalar units.
Give our team plan 5,000 units using that meter.

Configure team plan credits
The existing benefits are Compute Allowance (6,000 Compute Units, no rollover) and Workflow Starter Credits. Neither is attached to a product. I can safely prepare a hidden, unattached benefit using Workflow Units.
Which benefit should hold the 5,000 Workflow Units? Choices: Create a new team benefit; Update Compute Allowance; Update Workflow Starter Credits.
Should unused units roll over? Choices: No rollover; Enable rollover.

options.description: Prepare a hidden, unattached benefit for 5,000 Workflow Units.

options.label: Update Workflow Starter Credits

options.description: The balance resets on each grant.

values: Create a new benefit called Vector Team Credits.

messages.text:
Details for Configure team plan credits:
Which benefit should hold the 5,000 Workflow Units?: Create a new benefit called Vector Team Credits.
Should unused units roll over?: No rollover
Vector Team Credits is saved as a hidden, unattached benefit with 5,000 Workflow Units and no rollover.
Make that 7,500 units and keep everything else.
Vector Team Credits now has 7,500 Workflow Units. It remains hidden, uses the same meter, has no rollover, and is unattached.
What did we save?
Saved Vector Team Credits as a hidden Meter Credits benefit with 7,500 Workflow Units, no rollover, and no product attachment or grants.
Is any real usage being billed yet?
No. The credits benefit is not attached to any product and has no benefit grants, so there is no evidence that real usage is being billed yet.
Show me Home.
Home is open. The workspace overview shows a $0 available balance and no payouts yet.
